answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and place them at the bottom; shuffle the nine II cards and deal five above them; shuffle the three I cards and deal one on top. The resulting deck has 1 I, 5 II and 4 III. Return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: Create the Conflict Deck

answers.answer: A human starts at 1 VP in a four-player game and 0 VP in a three-player game; starts with two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; starts with 3 troops in their garrison and 9 in supply; and takes 1 water in either game.
answers.evidence: Setup: Score track on 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents on Leader; three troops in garrison, remaining nine in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain, but after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of that phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed for the Reveal turn, not cards played on Agent turns. Clean Up moves all cards in front of you from both types of turn to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns; Reveal Turn: Resolve Reveal Effects and Clean Up

answers.answer: No. Pay entry costs immediately before resolving any effects of the space or played card, so the Agent-box effect cannot fund the entry cost. One card sends only one Agent, using one Agent icon. A card without Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay any costs ... before resolving any effects ... one card can't send multiple Agents; no Agent icons ... only ... Reveal turn.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all three troops recruited during this turn plus up to two from the four already in the garrison, for at most five. At a non-Combat space, you cannot deploy units. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison before deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying Units: recruits from supply to garrison; Combat space permits any/all recruited this turn plus up to two from garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to a space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; it does not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to ignore another player's Agent at the destination. Gather Intelligence may be chosen just after placing your Agent and before receiving space/card effects, to recall a connected Spy and draw a card. The same Spy cannot do both on one placement, though two different Spies can be used for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence. The summary does not specify a separate later decision point for choosing to Gather Intelligence beyond that placement timing.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy Agent icon ... do not recall; Infiltrate ... occupied by another player; Gather Intelligence ... immediately after placing ... cannot recall the same Spy to both.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops give 4, one sandworm gives 3, and four revealed swords give 4. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. A player must have at least one unit in the Conflict to participate in the Combat Intrigue window.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop = 2, sandworm = 3, revealed sword = 1; last unit removed means strength 0. Combat Intrigue: players with at least one unit.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you acting again; the window closes once all players involved pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison) and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: not required to pass just because you passed earlier; resolve after consecutive passes. Resolve Combat cleanup.

answers.answer: In both three- and four-player games, tied players for first each receive the second reward, and nobody wins the Conflict or takes its card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: any number tie for first ... second reward ... no one wins or takes card. Resolve Combat: 0 strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: Having one or more sandworms doubles rewards once; two worms do not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on won Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 3 spice to gain 1 VP, you may pay 3 spice for 1 VP or pay 6 spice for 2 VP under the doubled reward.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more; control and battle icons excluded; may pay cost a second time (3 spice for 1 VP or 6 for 2).

answers.answer: When you win and take a Conflict card into your supply, check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card in your supply with the same icon. If there is a match, you must flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame, the wild icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply, also for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; lose it below 2 and regain it upon returning to 2. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if Influence falls below 4 and gained again on returning to 4. The first player to 4 also gets the Alliance token and 1 VP, which is lost with the token. Tying the holder at 4 does not steal the Alliance; an opponent must rise higher (with additional transfer rules when the holder loses Influence).
answers.evidence: Victory Points: Faction Influence; tying the current holder does not steal Alliance.

answers.answer: Persuasion may be spent before, between or after Reveal effects during your Reveal turn. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources for one card and split a source across multiple cards. The Row is refilled immediately, so you may buy the replacement if able. Acquired cards go face up in your discard pile and are not used immediately.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: may use Persuasion before, between or after effects; Acquiring Cards

answers.answer: During Makers, add 1 spice to each Maker space without an Agent; visiting a Maker space collects all bonus spice there. Deep Desert costs 3 water and Hagga Basin 1 water; their worm choices require Maker Hooks, while their base spice alternatives are 4 and 2 respectively. Hooks are not spent. A worm cannot be summoned to a Conflict protected by the Shield Wall; removing the Wall allows summoning to any Conflict. Sandworms go directly into your quadrant of the Conflict and can never be put in a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers; Sandworms; Maker spaces in Board Space Guide; Shield Wall

answers.answer: At the end of a round, if any player has 10 or more VP or the Conflict deck is empty, Endgame is triggered. Players may first play and resolve Endgame Intrigue, then compare VP. Ties break by spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: Game end

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup starts with two contracts face up and the remaining 18 of the 20 standard contracts face down in the bank. Add four Intrigue cards to the Intrigue deck and four Imperium cards to the Imperium deck. Shaddam Corrino IV is optional. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts stay in the box and are not part of standard CHOAM setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: Setup changes; 10 contrasting-back contracts ... leave them in the box.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts and replace it from the bank face up; if all contracts have been taken, it gives 2 Solari instead. Harvest is completed by visiting a Maker space and gaining the listed spice amount during that turn, counting all sources; Immediate completes as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts; Completing contracts

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a space after sending your Agent there this turn, you must wait until a future turn; you must have held it when placing the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its rewards, then flip the token face down and leave it in your supply. The contract effect resolves as another Agent-turn effect, in any order with space and Agent-box effects.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts; FAQ & Rulings: Contract completion is mandatory

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. It receives the Ornithopter Objective; the humans randomly receive the other two eligible Objectives, and the human with the First Player marker on their Objective starts. Order is First Player human, Rival, other human. The Rival takes Agent turns while it has Agents and never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules — Setup; Agent turns

answers.answer: The Rival ignores an occupied Hagal destination and reveals again. On a two-destination card it uses only the destination matching current conditions (Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping; Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner); if occupied, it reveals another card. It ignores normal space costs and effects and applies only the revealed Hagal effects. A Place Spy card uses an empty post of its specified type or ignores placement if none exists, then reveals another card. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, reshuffle immediately and continue.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns; Spies and Schemes

answers.answer: For three or four players, omit Objectives whose 1–3P/4/6P marking does not match the player count, shuffle the eligible cards, and give each player one at random. The player whose Objective shows the First Player marker takes it. Shaddam may be used only with the CHOAM Module.
answers.evidence: Setup: Shuffle the Objective cards ... marking doesn't match your player count; Shaddam only with CHOAM.

answers.answer: Bank resources and sandworms are not meant to be limited; if they run out, make any convenient substitution. If your personal troop supply runs out, you cannot recruit more until some troops return there. The summary identifies the bank as holding Solari, spice, water and sandworms, but does not explicitly state where resource payments are placed.
answers.evidence: Setup: bank ... not meant to be limited — make any convenient substitution; Recruiting: can't recruit until troops return to supply.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. Round Start reveals a Conflict card, then each player draws five cards. If Endgame is not triggered at Recall, players recall Agents to their Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and start the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Player Reference: Round

answers.answer: Yes. Board-space effects, Agent-box effects and Faction Influence may be resolved in any order. But entry costs and requirements must be met before resolving effects, so Influence from that visit cannot meet its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn; Influence-requirement spaces

answers.answer: No. An optional arrow cost/effect may be declined and may be paid only once per turn, except a doubled Conflict reward. Most effects are mandatory; exceptions include “may,” optional arrow costs and the optional black-X trash icon. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ & Rulings: Mandatory effects and costs

answers.answer: Place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If no Spies remain in supply, you may first recall one for no effect. If a placement effect specifies an Agent icon, the post must connect to a space bearing that icon or you cannot place the Spy.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts

answers.answer: No, Infiltrate is for sending to a space occupied by another player, not your own Agent. You cannot use a Spy without playing a card for an Agent turn; a Spy Agent icon accesses a connected space without recalling the Spy. You cannot recall one Spy for both effects on one placement, and cannot use two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on one placement.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts; FAQ & Rulings: Spies

answers.answer: Control is gained by winning the Conflict for Arrakeen, Spice Refinery or Imperial Basin; place your Control marker there, replacing an opponent's. The controller gets the location bonus whenever anyone visits it: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. When a Conflict at a location you control is revealed, you may deploy one defensive troop from your supply to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control

answers.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the first-place Conflict winner keeps their rewards and card, with no further rewards. Players tied for third receive nothing. If three or more tie for first in four-player play, they each get the second reward and no other rewards. If three players tie for first in a three-player game, they each get second reward and there are no other rewards; nobody takes the Conflict card.
answers.evidence: Combat ties

answers.answer: With three distinct positive strengths in a normal three-player Conflict, first, second and third place receive their respective rewards. The Rival follows normal two-/three-player reward and tie rules when it participates; it has no special placement reward rule stated here.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat; Required Rival Rules: Combat cleanup and two-/three-player reward and tie rules apply normally.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turns; Combat Intrigues during Combat; Endgame Intrigues at the end of the game. Keep Intrigues face down, separate from your deck; played cards are discarded face up after resolving, and unplayed ones remain held. If the Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle its discard pile to form a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards; FAQ & Rulings: Draw timing

answers.answer: An ordinary discard cannot be an Intrigue unless the instruction specifies otherwise. Secrets gives you one Intrigue at random from each opponent holding four or more. The summary does not specify the source zone for an ordinary discard instruction, so that part is unsupported.
answers.evidence: Discarding; Intrigue cards: Steal Intrigue icon

answers.answer: Trash effects may remove cards from hand, discard pile or in play. Ordinary cards go to the box and Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it is a cost or the card directs you to trash itself. The Spice Must Flow's acquire VP is retained even if the card is later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing; FAQ & Rulings: Victory

answers.answer: Acquire-box effects resolve once at the moment the card is acquired. When unable to draw because your deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue drawing. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of the Reveal turn and cannot be carried over.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed for Reveal remain face up and in play until Clean Up (unless trashed). Fremen Bond needs one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate one another regardless of play order. They cease to be in play at Clean Up.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent placed this turn; you can use the recalled Agent on another Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop goes from the Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” includes zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ & Rulings: Combat and troops

answers.answer: An effect granting two free-choice Influence must put both gains in the same Faction; it cannot split them. An Alliance icon requires that you hold that Faction's Alliance token. A minimum-Influence effect requires the stated Influence with the specified Faction.
answers.evidence: Influence

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied, a formerly tied player takes the Alliance; if multiple players were tied, the former holder chooses which receives it. If the holder falls to 3 or lower, they lose the Alliance; if nobody has 4 or more to take it, return it to the board. The VP follows the token.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Alliance loss

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used that turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, then you draw five additional cards. A Plot Intrigue played earlier with a Reveal effect stays face up until the effect applies, then is used and discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Draw timing

answers.answer: No. “When you win” Intrigues cannot be played after tying for first, since no one wins the Conflict. If you receive one as a reward for an outright win, you may play it immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Combat and troops

answers.answer: If VP and all four resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed track's 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Victory

answers.answer: No. Fulfill all contracts held for the same space with one Agent placement, and you must have held them when sending that Agent. Each contract is another effect of that Agent turn and may resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Contract completion is mandatory

answers.answer: No, Shaddam does not begin with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts; Sardaukar Commander lets him choose one instead of a generally available contract when acquiring a contract. Emperor of the Known Universe applies immediately when playing Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the round.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Shaddam

answers.answer: Feyd's Training token starts on the leftmost space of his Leader track and remains at the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica begins face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica; Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications; FAQ & Rulings

answers.answer: Moving from 1 to 3 reaches 2 and triggers the ability. You can reach 2 with the same Faction again after losing Influence and later moving up to 2; moving down through 2 does not count. Moving Spacing Guild's Favor from in play to discard during Clean Up does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Lady Margot Fenring / Princess Irulan; Spacing Guild's Favor

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade icon, has no cost, draws a card and gives a contract with CHOAM or 2 Solari without it (including when none remain). Dutiful Service uses the Emperor icon, has no cost, gives 1 Emperor Influence and gives a contract with CHOAM or 2 Solari without it. Both are actual Faction board spaces, so each visit automatically advances that Faction's track by one in addition to listed effects.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Accept Contract and Dutiful Service; Influence

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, Combat; recruit one troop and draw one card, with the controller gaining 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, Combat; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, Combat; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide

answers.answer: Deep Desert (Spice Trade, Combat) costs 3 water; Hagga Basin (Spice Trade, Combat) costs 1 water. Both collect all bonus spice. Deep Desert then offers 4 base spice or, with Hooks, two sandworms; Hagga offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Hooks are retained, not spent, when summoning.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; Maker spaces; FAQ & Rulings: Spies

answers.answer: Sietch Tabr is a City Combat space requiring 2+ Fremen Influence. Choose either: take a Maker Hooks token if you lack one, recruit one troop and gain 1 water; or gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The Shield Wall option does not also give a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Sietch Tabr

answers.answer: High Council is Landsraad and costs 5 Solari each visit. The first visit places your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gives 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Later visits give 2 spice, draw an Intrigue and recruit three troops. It is not marked as a Combat space.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: High Council

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone has one and 6 after anyone (including a Rival) obtains one. Each player may visit only once per game. The third Agent is available in the current round and the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Swordmaster

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses the Landsraad icon, requires 2+ Emperor Influence and costs 3 Solari. It lets you discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, then recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not itself grant Emperor Influence; the recalled Agent is another Agent on the board, not the one sent this turn.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Privilege; Recall Agent icon; Influence

answers.answer: Shipping uses the Spice Trade icon, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence and costs 3 spice. It gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; the Influence need not be with the Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Shipping

answers.answer: Gather Support (Landsraad, not Combat) lets you choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari; recruit two troops either way, and gain 1 water if you paid. Spice Refinery (City, Combat) lets you pay 0 or 1 spice to gain 2 or 4 Solari respectively; its controller also gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide

answers.answer: Heighliner: 5 spice, +1 Guild Influence, recruit five; Combat. Desert Tactics: 1 water, +1 Fremen Influence, recruit one and optionally trash a card; Combat. Sardaukar: 4 spice, +1 Emperor Influence, draw an Intrigue and recruit four; not listed as Combat. Only Heighliner and Desert Tactics are among the listed Combat spaces with Factions; Sardaukar is not marked Combat.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; Recruiting & Deploying Units lists the three Faction Combat spaces as Heighliner, Desert Tactics and Fremkit.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall is Landsraad, no cost: draw an Intrigue; gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is still there. Espionage is Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice: gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card and place a Spy. Deliver Supplies is Spacing Guild, no cost: gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water. They are not marked as Combat spaces.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn; it may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: False Orders; Litany Against Fear

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If it has not been acquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Manipulate

answers.answer: The Rival gets a color, four cubes at the bottom of Influence tracks, three troops in garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply with Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies, and 1 water; score and Combat marker begin at 0. Keep the 2P Reshuffle card in House Hagal. The Rival's 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall and it can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup; first paragraph

answers.answer: As soon as the Rival's Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water total reaches its printed Swordmaster value, it spends that many resources and takes its third Agent, usable this round. It spends Solari first, then spice, Intrigue cards, then water, keeping leftovers. A Rival Swordmaster also reduces the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Resources and Swordmaster; Board Space Guide: Swordmaster

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, it spends each set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP. A mixed total of seven resources does not qualify; the specified sets are separate.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Resources and Swordmaster

answers.answer: The Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by the leftmost Faction priority icon. It gains/loses VP at 2 Influence and gets Alliance VP like a human, but receives no resource bonus for reaching 4. A numbered Hagal Influence icon refers to that position in its priority list.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Resources and Swordmaster; Agent turns

answers.answer: It uses only the destination selected by the current condition; if that destination is occupied, it reveals another card and does not use the other destination. Conditions are Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping and Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns

answers.answer: At a Combat space a Rival deploys all troops newly recruited by the Hagal card plus up to two available troops from its garrison, even if the card recruited none. Troops recruited at a noncombat space go to its garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus not met is ignored but does not prevent placement.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns

answers.answer: Unless a post type is specified, the Rival uses the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. A specified Place Spy post is used if empty, otherwise placement is ignored and another Hagal card is revealed. Placing its third and final supply Spy recalls the other two and triggers its printed Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Spies and Schemes

answers.answer: If the Scheme recruits troops before the Agent placement and the Rival then visits a Combat space that same turn, those troops deploy too. If Place Spy finds no legal post, it ignores placement and reveals another Hagal card because no Agent was sent.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Spies and Schemes

answers.answer: The Rival always collects all bonus spice at a visited Maker space. At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, it summons one or two worms instead of base spice if it has Hooks and the Conflict permits worms; otherwise it takes the base spice (2 at Hagga, 4 at Deep Desert). A protected Conflict prevents worms; accumulated bonus spice is still collected. Hooks are not spent.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Maker spaces; FAQ & Rulings: Spies

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal a Hagal card in turn order and add only its bottom swords to strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then get their normal Combat Intrigue window. A unit-free Rival gets no such bonus.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Combat

answers.answer: Yes. The Rival gains control bonuses when any player visits its controlled space, gets the defensive troop from supply when that Conflict is revealed, gains battle-icon VP and doubles rewards with worms. It always takes optional Conflict VP if it can pay or recall the required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Combat

answers.answer: During Resolve Reveal Effects, total and announce strength and set the marker at any point; update it as needed during the Reveal turn. If strength exceeds 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: Resolve Reveal Effects; Actions: Strength

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on an Agent turn to send an Agent, not when you merely reveal it. Cards of any type can override the usual rules of the game.
answers.evidence: Setup: Leader abilities; Overview

answers.answer: The Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. It is not automatically the Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence action; those are separate optional recalls for their stated effects.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts

answers.answer: The trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction cannot discard an Intrigue unless it specifically says so.
answers.evidence: Trashing; Discarding

answers.answer: When a Conflict reward's one Influence is doubled by your worm, the two gains may go to the same Faction or two different Factions. By contrast, one effect that grants two free-choice Influence must place both in the same Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling; Influence

answers.answer: The Rival resolves the Signet Ring ability printed on its own Rival card as directed by its House Hagal card. It does not need a human Signet Ring card or a Reveal turn; Rivals take Agent turns and never Reveal.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: follow its printed Signet Ring and Scheme abilities; Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
